what: Wall-clock for a batch of K independent folds on ONE GPU. Four batch sizes, same machine, same engine, same inputs as scripts/scaling_benchmark.py writes.
why: It isolates the per-run fixed cost from the per-fold cost. Batch sharding across N devices makes every device pay the fixed cost separately, so that split is what decides whether adding cards helps.
hardware: 1x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090, 24 GB. The only GPU available to this project.
inputs: K copies of GFP (UniProt P42212), one substitution apart so no fold is a cache hit. Single chains. Empty MSA declared in the FASTA header, so no network.

fit.note: Four points is a small fit and the residual at copies=4 is 5.4 s, so treat these as the right order of magnitude rather than as precise constants. The qualitative result -- a fixed cost several times the marginal cost of one fold -- is not sensitive to that.

predicted_efficiency_8_devices.comment: From the fit above, not measured. speedup = t(K,1)/t(K,N) with t(K,N) = fixed + per_fold*K/N. A ceiling: it ignores host memory, PCIe and filesystem contention, which only reduce it.

what_this_does_not_measure: More than one device. There is one card here; every multi-device number on this page is a prediction derived from single-card measurements, and is labelled as such.
Two-chain complexes. These are single chains, which are smaller and faster per fold than a real binder-target assembly.
Context-parallel folding of one oversized complex, which no installed engine supports.
